title: The substrate parameter as a measure of non-commutativity
html:
The substrate parameter q governs the non-commutativity of the algebraic substrate. At q = 1, the algebra becomes commutative and the quantum structure degenerates to its classical shadow. The pair (q, \hbar_q) parametrizes the deviation of A from commutativity: in the classical limit q o 1, \hbar_q o 0 recovers the commutative coordinate ring and the smooth manifold geometry.

The invertibility condition q e 0 ensures that A is a genuine Hopf algebra with well-defined antipode. Because \hbar_q e 0 whenever q e 1, the non-commutative regime always carries a non-trivial quantum scale.
